source_text: εἰ συντετάξονται τοῖς ἀλλογενέσιν οἱ πάροικοί τε καὶ μισθωτοὶ καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ὡς ἀπωτάτω, σὺν ἐκείνοις ἔσονται· μόνον δὲ οὐχὶ καὶ ἀδελφὰ νοσοῦντες ἐγκλήματα, τὴν ὁμοφυᾶ δικαίως ὑποστήσονται δίκην. Ἀνεῖσθαι δὲ δεῖν τοῖς οἰκείοις ἔφη τῶν ἁγίων τὴν μέθεξιν. Φάγονται γὰρ, φησὶν, οἱ τῶν ἱερέων οἰκογενεῖς, καὶ ὃν ἂν ἐκπρίαιντο τυχὸν, ἔκκτητόν τε καὶ ἀργυρώνητον καὶ οἰκογενῆ που λέγων, τὸν ἐν πίστει γνήσιον, καὶ οἰκεῖον ἐν πνεύματι, καὶ τιμῆς ἠγορασμένον, κατὰ τὸν μακάριον Παῦλον. «Χριστὸς γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νομοῦ, γενόμενος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα,» κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Προσεπιτάττει δὲ ὅτι καὶ θυγάτηρ ἀνθρώπου ἱερέως, ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἀλλογενεῖ, αὕτη τῶν ἀπαρχῶν τῶν ἁγίων οὐ φάγεται. Τὸν μὲν οἰκεῖον ἐκτετίμηκεν ἐναργῶς, μεταλαχεῖν ἐφιεὶς τῶν ἁγίων, ὡς γνήσιον· πλὴν ὅτι τοῖς ἔχουσι τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἰκειότητα, παραιτητέον εὖ μάλα τὸ προσκολλᾶσθαι φιλεῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ πίστιν ἢ τρόπον οἰκείοις, μήτε μὴν τὸ οἱονεὶ συγγενὲς πεπλουτηκόσιν ἐξ ἀρετῆς, οὐκ ἀσυμφανὲς ἂν γένοιτο τοῖς ἐθέλουσι πολυπραγμονεῖν τῶν ἱερῶν Γραμμάτων τὴν πίστιν. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν τοῖς ἤδη προανεγνωσμένοις ἀκάθαρτον μὲν ἐποίει τὸν λεπρὸν, καὶ αὖ ἐπὶ τούτῳ τὸν γονοῤῥυᾶ, μολυσμοῦ δὲ καὶ ἀκαθαρσίας τῆς ἐπ' αὐτοῖς ἐτίθει μέτοχον τὸν ἀγχοῦ γεγονότα, καὶ οἱονεὶ συνημμένον ἐξ ἐπαφῆς· οὕτω κἀνθάδε τὴν ἱερέως θυγατέρα φησὶ, κἂν εἰ ἔχοι τυχὸν τὸ συγγενὲς ἅγιον, οὐδὲν ἐντεῦθεν ὠφεληθήσεσθαι, συνημμένην ἑτέρῳ, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἀλλογενεῖ, τῷ μηδαμόθεν οἰκείῳ, μήτε μὴν ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραήλ. Ὁ μὲν οὖν τῆς ἱστορίας ἐν τούτοις ᾖ λόγος. Παροισθέντος δὲ ἡμῖν εἰς θεωρίαν πνευματικὴν τοῦ νόμου, φαμὲν ὅτι θυγατέρα φησὶν ἱερέως, τὴν ἐξ ὕδατός τε καὶ πνεύματος ἀναγεννηθεῖσαν ψυχὴν δυνάμει Χριστοῦ, καὶ διὰ πίστεως κεκλημένην εἰς ἁγιασμόν· ἀλλ' ἔσται, φησὶ, καὶ ἡ τοιάδε τυχὸν τῶν ἁγίων ἀμέτοχος, εἰ γένοιτο ἀνθρώπῳ ἀλλογενεῖ, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, εἰ συνάπτοιτό τισι τοῖς οὐκ ἀληθῶς ἁγίοις, καὶ σχέσιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν πρὸς Θεὸν πνευματικήν· σώμασι μὲν οὖν σωματικὸς ἂν γένοιτο τῆς συναφείας ὁ τρόπος, πνεύμασι δὲ αὖ πνευματικός. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τίνας εἰς τοῦτο παρενεχθῆναί φαμεν; {ΚΥΡ.} Οὓς ὁ σεμνὸς τῆς σοφίας διησφαλίζετο λόγος, οὕτως ἔχων· «Υἱὲ, μή σε πλανήσωσιν ἄνδρες ἀσεβεῖς, μηδὲ βουληθῇς ἐὰν παρακαλέσωσί σε λέγοντες· Ἐλθὲ μεθ' ἡμῶν· κοινώνησον αἵματος.» Προσθήσομεν δὲ κἀκείνους, οἳ τῆς ὀρθῆς πίστεως ἀμαθῶς ἀπονενευκότες, ὀπίσω τρέχουσι σαρκὸς, τοὺς μὲν διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος οὐ προσιέμενοι λόγους, προσεσχηκότες δὲ πνεύμασι πλάνης, ἐν ὑποκρίσει ψευδολόγων, κεκαυστηριασμένων τὸν νοῦν. Οὗτοι τὴν πρὸς Χριστὸν οἰκειότητα παρωθούμενοι, γεγόνασι κατὰ τὸ ἀληθὲς ἀνθρώποις ἀλλογενέσι, καὶ σπερμάτων ἠνέσχοντο διαβολικῶν, καρποφοροῦντες ἐν πλάνῃ τὰ πλάνης
pass_a_gloss: [as far as came to the force of the law,] if the sojourners and hired men will be ranked with the foreigners and very far from the holy things, they will be with those; and all but sick with kindred charges, they will justly undergo the kindred penalty. And he said that the sharing of the holy things must be left open to those of the household. For they shall eat, he says, those born in the priests' house, and whomever they may perhaps buy, saying acquired and bought with silver and born in the house, the one genuine in faith, and of the household in spirit, and bought with a price, according to the blessed Paul. 'For Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us,' according to what is written. PALL.: True. CYR.: He further commands that also a daughter of a priest, if she becomes a foreign man's, this one shall not eat of the firstfruits of the holy things. He has clearly honoured the one of the household, allowing him to share in the holy things as genuine; except that for those having the close bond toward him, one must very much decline to love to cling to those not of the household according to faith or way, nor indeed to those rich, as it were, in kinship from virtue: this would not be unclear to those willing to search into the evidence of the sacred Scriptures. For as in what was read before he made unclean the leper, and in addition to him the one with a flux, and set as sharer in the defilement and uncleanness on them the one who came near, and as it were joined by touch: so here too he says that the priest's daughter, even if she should perhaps have the holy kinship, will be helped nothing from it, joined to another, that is, a foreigner, the one in no way of the household, nor from the blood of Israel. Let the account of the history in these things be thus. But the law having been brought across by us into spiritual contemplation, we say that by the daughter of a priest he means the soul reborn from water and spirit by the power of Christ, and called through faith to sanctification; but, he says, even such a one will perhaps be without share of the holy things, if she becomes a foreign man's, that is, if she is joined to some who are not truly holy, and have no spiritual relation to God; for to bodies the way of union would be bodily, but to spirits again spiritual. PALL.: And whom do we say were carried aside into this? CYR.: Those whom the solemn word of wisdom was making safe, holding thus: 'Son, let not ungodly men lead you astray, nor be willing if they call on you saying: Come with us; share in blood.' And we shall add those also who, having ignorantly turned away from the right faith, run after flesh, not admitting the words through the Holy Spirit, but having given heed to spirits of error, in the hypocrisy of liars, seared in the mind. These, thrusting aside the close bond toward Christ, have become in truth foreign men's, and have endured devilish seeds, bearing fruit in error the [works] of error
pass_b_english: Cyril: …if the sojourners and the hired servants are ranked with the foreigners, they will also be with them, as far as possible from the holy things; and since they are all but sick with kindred faults, they will justly suffer a penalty of the same kind. But he said that the sharing of the holy things must be left open to the members of the household. For those born in the priests’ households will eat, he says, and anyone they may happen to buy. By ‘acquired’, ‘bought with silver’ and ‘born in the house’ he means, I take it, the one who is genuine in faith, a member of the household in spirit, and bought with a price, as the blessed Paul says (1 Corinthians 6:20). For, as it is written, ‘Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us’ (Galatians 3:13).

Cyril: He further commands that if the daughter of a priest is married to a foreign man, she shall not eat of the firstfruits of the holy things (Leviticus 22:12). He has plainly honored the member of the household by allowing him to share in the holy things as one who is genuine. Yet those who have this close bond with the priest must firmly refuse to cling to people who are not their own by faith or by way of life and have not gained through virtue a kind of kinship with them; this will be clear enough to anyone willing to search the evidence of the sacred Scriptures. For just as in the passages already read he made the leper unclean, and with him the man with a discharge, and made the one who came near them, joined to them, as it were, by touch, a sharer in their defilement and uncleanness, so here too he says that the priest’s daughter, even if she happens to have a holy kinship, will gain nothing from it when she is joined to another, that is, to a foreigner, one who is in no way akin to her and not of the blood of Israel. Let this, then, be the historical sense. But when we carry the law over into spiritual contemplation, we say that by the priest’s daughter he means the soul that has been born again of water and the Spirit (John 3:5) by the power of Christ, and called through faith to sanctification. Yet even such a soul, he says, may have no share in the holy things if she is married to a foreign man, that is, if she joins herself to people who are not truly holy and have no spiritual bond with God. For bodies the manner of union would be bodily, but for spirits it is spiritual.
Palladius: And who, would we say, have been carried away into this?

Cyril: Those whom the solemn word of Wisdom sought to keep safe when it said: ‘My son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray, and do not consent if they urge you, saying: Come with us, share in blood’ (Proverbs 1:10–11). We will also add those who in their ignorance have turned away from the right faith and run after the flesh; who do not admit the words given through the Holy Spirit, but have given heed to spirits of error, through the hypocrisy of liars who are seared in their minds (1 Timothy 4:1–2). These have thrust aside their close bond with Christ, and in truth they have been married to foreign men; they have accepted the devil’s seed, and in error they bear as fruit the…

choices.why: μόνον δὲ οὐχί is taken as 'all but' (they are all but sick with kindred faults).

choices.term: πολυπραγμονεῖν τῶν ἱερῶν Γραμμάτων τὴν πίστιν
choices.why: πολυπραγμονεῖν τῶν ἱερῶν Γραμμάτων τὴν πίστιν: πίστις here taken as 'evidence' or 'proof' of Scripture, not personal faith.

Τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἰκειότητα rendered 'close bond with the priest' (αὐτόν = the priest of the law, read as Christ, as in §11 and at the end of §12); διησφαλίζετο means Wisdom sought to keep these people safe, not that it guarded against them.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, finishing §11's 'As far, then, as the force of the law goes…'. μόνον δὲ οὐχί is taken as 'all but' (they are all but sick with kindred faults). ἀνεῖσθαι rendered 'left open'. The household-and-purchase terms (ἔκκτητον, ἀργυρώνητον, οἰκογενῆ) gloss Leviticus 22:11, cited in §11. 'Bought with a price, as blessed Paul says' = 1 Corinthians 6:20 (also 7:23). 'Married to a foreign man' renders the idiom γίνεσθαι ἀνδρί (Leviticus 22:12, LXX θυγάτηρ ἀνθρώπου ἱερέως ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἀλλογενεῖ…οὐ φάγεται); the same idiom returns at the end (γεγόνασι… ἀνθρώποις ἀλλογενέσι), so it is rendered the same way there. πολυπραγμονεῖν τῶν ἱερῶν Γραμμάτων τὴν πίστιν: πίστις here taken as 'evidence' or 'proof' of Scripture, not personal faith. οἰκεῖον ἐν πνεύματι kept lowercase ('in spirit') as the contrast with blood kinship; in ἐξ ὕδατός τε καὶ πνεύματος (John 3:5) Spirit is capitalized. Proverbs 1:10–11 LXX; Cyril stops before the rest of verse 11 (κρύψωμεν δὲ εἰς γῆν ἄνδρα δίκαιον ἀδίκως). The phrase on false teachers follows 1 Timothy 4:1–2 closely, except that Cyril writes 'seared in their mind' (τὸν νοῦν) where Paul has 'conscience'; cited. Uncited loose echoes: 'run after the flesh' (2 Peter 2:10; Jude 7), 'devil's seed' (the tares, Matthew 13:25, 39), the body/spirit union contrast (1 Corinthians 6:16–17), 'called to sanctification' (1 Thessalonians 4:7). The section ends mid-phrase: καρποφοροῦντες ἐν πλάνῃ τὰ πλάνης | ἔργα καὶ ἀπωλείας (§13), so the English stops at 'in error they bear as fruit the…'; §13 should continue '…works of error and destruction'. Review: τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἰκειότητα rendered 'close bond with the priest' (αὐτόν = the priest of the law, read as Christ, as in §11 and at the end of §12); διησφαλίζετο means Wisdom sought to keep these people safe, not that it guarded against them.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [ὅσον ἧκεν εἰς νόμου δύναμιν,] εἰ συντετάξονται τοῖς ἀλλογενέσιν οἱ πάροικοί τε καὶ μισθωτοὶ and ὡς ἀπωτάτω τῶν ἁγίων, σὺν ἐκείνοις ἔσονται; μόνον οὐχὶ (all but) also νοσοῦντες ἀδελφὰ ἐγκλήματα, they will undergo (ὑποστήσονται) δικαίως τὴν ὁμοφυᾶ δίκην. He said ἀνεῖσθαι δεῖν (must be opened/allowed) τοῖς οἰκείοις ἡ μέθεξις τῶν ἁγίων. φάγονται οἱ τῶν ἱερέων οἰκογενεῖς, καὶ ὃν ἂν ἐκπρίαιντο; ἔκκτητον καὶ ἀργυρώνητον καὶ οἰκογενῆ λέγων = τὸν ἐν πίστει γνήσιον, οἰκεῖον ἐν πνεύματι, τιμῆς ἠγορασμένον, per Paul; Χριστὸς ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου, γενόμενος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα. PALL: ἀληθές. CYR: προσεπιτάττει: θυγάτηρ ἀνθρώπου ἱερέως, ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἀλλογενεῖ, οὐ φάγεται τῶν ἀπαρχῶν τῶν ἁγίων. τὸν οἰκεῖον ἐκτετίμηκεν ἐναργῶς, ἐφιεὶς μεταλαχεῖν ὡς γνήσιον; yet for those ἔχοντες τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἰκειότητα, παραιτητέον εὖ μάλα τὸ προσκολλᾶσθαι φιλεῖν to those μὴ κατὰ πίστιν ἢ τρόπον οἰκεῖοι, nor πεπλουτηκόσι τὸ οἱονεὶ συγγενὲς ἐξ ἀρετῆς: οὐκ ἀσυμφανές to those willing πολυπραγμονεῖν τῶν ἱερῶν Γραμμάτων τὴν πίστιν. As ἐν τοῖς προανεγνωσμένοις he made unclean τὸν λεπρόν and τὸν γονορρυᾶ, and set τὸν ἀγχοῦ γεγονότα, οἱονεὶ συνημμένον ἐξ ἐπαφῆς, as μέτοχον of their μολυσμὸς καὶ ἀκαθαρσία: so here the ἱερέως θυγάτηρ, κἂν ἔχοι τὸ συγγενὲς ἅγιον, οὐδὲν ὠφεληθήσεσθαι, συνημμένην ἑτέρῳ = ἀλλογενεῖ, μηδαμόθεν οἰκείῳ, not ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραήλ. Ὁ τῆς ἱστορίας λόγος: thus. Παροισθέντος τοῦ νόμου εἰς θεωρίαν πνευματικήν: θυγάτηρ ἱερέως = ψυχὴ ἀναγεννηθεῖσα ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος δυνάμει Χριστοῦ, διὰ πίστεως κεκλημένη εἰς ἁγιασμόν; ἀλλ' even she ἀμέτοχος τῶν ἁγίων εἰ γένοιτο ἀνθρώπῳ ἀλλογενεῖ = εἰ συνάπτοιτο to those οὐκ ἀληθῶς ἁγίοις, σχέσιν οὐκ ἔχουσι πρὸς Θεὸν πνευματικήν; for σώματα the τρόπος τῆς συναφείας σωματικός, for πνεύματα πνευματικός. PALL: τίνας εἰς τοῦτο παρενεχθῆναί φαμεν; CYR: those whom ὁ σεμνὸς τῆς σοφίας λόγος διησφαλίζετο (guarded): Υἱέ, μή σε πλανήσωσιν ἄνδρες ἀσεβεῖς, μηδὲ βουληθῇς ἐὰν παρακαλέσωσι: ἐλθὲ μεθ' ἡμῶν, κοινώνησον αἵματος. Add those τῆς ὀρθῆς πίστεως ἀμαθῶς ἀπονενευκότες, ὀπίσω τρέχοντες σαρκός, not προσιέμενοι τοὺς διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος λόγους, προσεσχηκότες πνεύμασι πλάνης, ἐν ὑποκρίσει ψευδολόγων, κεκαυστηριασμένων τὸν νοῦν. These, παρωθούμενοι τὴν πρὸς Χριστὸν οἰκειότητα, γεγόνασι κατὰ τὸ ἀληθὲς ἀνθρώποις ἀλλογενέσι, ἠνέσχοντο σπερμάτων διαβολικῶν, καρποφοροῦντες ἐν πλάνῃ τὰ πλάνης [ἔργα] (continues in §13).
